{"type":"text","timestamp":1794722672913,"sessionID":"ses_e22347127ffeSu9dweykea9bAd","part":{"id":"prt_1ddceb0f7001blwEtr6lYk6Qu6","messageID":"msg_1ddcea0d8001fjk5Msc6Z89q25","sessionID":"ses_e22347127ffeSu9dweykea9bAd","type":"text","text":"The lid now opens to the full 110° with no overlap and at least 0.35 mm clearance at every step from 10°. Every gate, `S1_opening` and both printability checks pass in the one `test_fit` run. `S3_minimal_change` also passes, but its score depends on the best-known fix, which isn't shown. I submitted, so the result is final.\n\n**Cause:** the structural ribs under the lid knuckles swung into the rear wall of the enclosure. The original lid stopped working at 37°.\n\n**Fix:** I made one change, and only to the enclosure. I cut a small pocket into the outer face of the rear wall at each of the three knuckle positions. Each pocket is open at the top and sized to the swept path of its rib plus clearance. The three cuts remove 37.6 mm³ in total, and nothing was added. The lid was not touched.\n\nEach pocket runs about 6.4 mm along the hinge axis, 3.0 mm down from the wall top and 1.0 mm into the wall. The wall that remains is about 1.7 mm thick, above the 1.2 mm minimum, and the seal band on the inner side is untouched. The seal contact stays 1.72 mm wide.\n\nI did not try to shrink the pockets further, so some of the minimal-change score may be left on the table.","time":{"start":1794722672887,"end":1794722672909}}}
